bull_bear.body: Prioritizing capex for capacity expansion (INR 100cr FY26); funding via borrowings currently; equity raise not ruled out for future WC needs; no dividend policy mentioned; M&A focus on tech (Molsieve acquisition) to enable hydrogen entry
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Biomass tariff reversal outcome (if denied, EBITDA margin drops to 16-18%); execution delays in new capacity ramp-up; hydrogen revenue realization delayed beyond 6-9 months; geopolitical tariff risks (though management claims <10% product exposure); working capital strain from rising inventory days (247 days)
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, proactive, and transparent; management emphasizes execution, capacity utilization, and strategic diversification; clear articulation of catalysts (Anjar, hydrogen, biomass ruling); no defensiveness on margins or guidance
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Anjar facility’s capacity expansion is not just volume-driven — it’s enabling higher-value metallurgy and reducing logistics cost, improving margins beyond simple scale; Molsieve’s 99.9999% purity tech is a defensible IP moat in hydrogen purification, not just a product add-on
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- ₹300 Cr preferential issue completed during Q1 FY27 at ₹502/share, anchored by WhiteOak, Kotak, 360 ONE and ValueQuest.
- ₹225 Cr of the proceeds earmarked for debt repayment, "strengthening balance sheet and lowering finance cost outgo"; management expects it to "materially reduce leverage and finance costs, improve return ratios".
- The additional pellet capacity "is proposed to be housed under the InVIT, enabling efficient capital deployment".
- Shareholding pattern: Promoters 65%, FII + DII 19%, Public 16%.
- Deleveraging is listed as a Vision 2030 operating-efficiency lever, but the slide's own wording is internally inconsistent: "Debt reduction <2x → ~3.5x by FY30".
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Piping division: 86.9% of revenue, up 30.4% YoY; Biomass power: contributing negative margin impact of ~200bps; Green Hydrogen: early-stage, no revenue yet, but bidding active via Molsieve’s ultra-pure purification tech; High-wall seamless pipes: new plant commissioning Jan 2026
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tariff risk on US exports | Other Indian piping exporters with higher US exposure | loser | High | DEEDEV has <2% US exposure vs peers; HSN code advantage shields 90% of exports |
| Lack of hydrogen purification IP | Generic EPC players in green hydrogen | loser | High | DEEDEV’s Molsieve tech enables ultra-pure H2 — a key differentiator in a nascent market |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Founded 1988 by Mr. K. L. Bansal; deck claims "Market leader in India by installed capacity", "Amongst Top 5 players in the world by installed process piping capacity" and 38 years of operational experience.
- Moat framed as "Strong entry and qualification barriers": DEE qualifies through customer audits and wins work via technical-commercial bidding, with "Strong engineering depth (730+ specialists) creates high entry barriers, pricing power, and customer retention".
- Serves Oil & Gas, Power (including Nuclear) and Chemical sectors across "27+ countries" and "4+ continents", including Canada, the USA, Italy and Japan; tagline "Make every customer a repeat customer".
- Material expertise cited in complex metals — carbon steel, stainless steel, super duplex stainless steel, alloy steel, and high-performance materials like Inconel and Hastelloy.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Leadership] New CFO appointed in FY26 — Mr. Brham Prakash Yadav; leadership also lists Pankaj Agarwal (COO), Ranjan Kumar Sarangi (CS & Compliance Officer), K. Kris (CEO – DEE Piping Systems, Thailand) and B S Jangra (CEO – Malwa Power Private Limited).
- [Tariff order] Malwa Power (Muktsar) tariff revised from ₹3.50/kWh, with retrospective recovery of ~₹5.14 crore in FY26 and an APTEL appeal ongoing for further optimization. The deck gives conflicting revised-tariff figures — see notes.
- [Large order] Secured a ₹387 Cr piping order from BPCL, described as "the largest domestic Oil & Gas mandate"; FY26 wins included ₹170 Cr domestic power orders, a USD 40 Mn+ LOI into global OEM supply chains (conversion underway), ₹173 Cr multi-geography orders, a ₹58 Cr first seamless pipe order, a ₹20 Cr Taiwan LOI and ₹70 Cr Thailand inflows in March.
- [Market data] Capital market overview as of August 2026: CMP ₹658 (as on 04.08.26), 52-week high/low ₹760 / ₹183, market capitalisation ₹4,952 Cr, 7.52 Cr shares outstanding.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margin at 16.0% in Q1; would have been 18%+ without biomass tariff loss; cost savings from Anjar facility reducing Palwal load and material handling costs; raw material cost pressure offset by higher-value metallurgy and project mix
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue: INR 1,300cr for FY26 (subject to biomass tariff outcome); EBITDA Margin: 19-20% (if biomass tariff restored); Order Inflow: INR 1,200cr expected by March FY26; Capex/Commissioning: INR 100cr total FY26; Anjar expansion commissioned by Aug 2025; High-wall seamless pipe plant to commence by Jan 2026
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: INR 12,267cr as of July 31, 2025; Expected to grow to INR 1,500cr+ by March FY26; 45% from Oil & Gas, rest from Power and exports
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Green hydrogen EPC market (700-1500 Nm3/day units) with low competition; potential to scale beyond modular systems into BOO models; export diversification beyond USA to EU, Japan, Canada; biomass tariff reversal unlocks margin upside
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Strong Q1FY26 performance driven by 21% revenue growth and 44.7% EBITDA margin expansion, with capacity expansion at Anjar ahead of schedule and strategic entry into green hydrogen via Molsieve acquisition and Clean-Tech partnership creating a new high-margin growth pillar.

open.item: Expect first hydrogen business/bids to convert in 6-9 months; detailed hydrogen revenue projections to be given in the next or next-to-next earnings call.
Around INR25-30 crores capex already done in Q1 FY26; expected total capital cost of around INR100 crores within the financial year to reach planned process piping and seamless piping capacities.

Malwa Power impairment audit qualification expected to be resolved to a clean opinion by the third quarter (of FY27), with no impairment or financial contingency anticipated given upward tariff revision and pellet plant.

Expecting more than INR2,000 crores of order inflow in FY27, with ~60% from the power sector and the rest from oil and gas; 60-65% domestic and 35-40% export (contingent on BHEL orders materialising).
Committed to at least INR1,500 crores revenue in FY27 as a conservative target, with likely upside beyond that given order traction.
Expecting around 65-70% of FY27 revenue from the power sector (thermal from India and HRSG from abroad); power orders currently ~INR1,000-1,200 cr in order book.
Targeting working capital cycle of around 180 days in FY27 (first target, eventually 150 days): inventory days down 15-20 days, debtor days ~95-100, payable days improved to above 70-75.

Malwa Power tariff revised up to Rs. 5.22/KwH from Rs. 3.5/KwH with ~INR5.52 cr retrospective recovery; combined power + biomass pellet revenue expected ~INR47.71 cr in FY27; biomass pellet facility to offset cash burn and stabilise segment.
FY27 capex to be limited to around INR20-30 crores (remaining/maintenance), though a new capacity expansion (e.g. for nuclear) is on the drawing board and could add capex.
Expect Anjar fabrication facility to reach optimal/expected utilisation in FY27 and the seamless plant to ramp to around 60-70%.
Guided consolidated EBITDA margin of above 19% going forward.
Targeting FY27 order book of ~INR2,000 crores funded from improved internal cash flow without new debt (unless a sudden ~INR1,000 crore order block arises).
Going forward in FY27, core business (piping and fabrication) EBITDA margin expected in the 18% to 20% range.
High-wall thickness pipe plant expected to generate around INR200 crores of revenue at full capacity (asset turnover roughly 2x in first fiscal).
Seamless pipe used for backward integration adds to EBITDA via purchase margin; when sold independently as commodity, margin expected around 20%.
Conservative growth estimate of 20% CAGR, with possibility of 25-30% given HRSG/power traction.
Existing facilities (post remaining capex) can generate around INR2,500 crores revenue; target of INR2,500 crores by FY30 (could be earlier with stronger order flow).
Reiterated 3x revenue growth target over 3-5 years (by FY30), driven mainly by the Anjar expansion.
Maintains long-term guidance of a threefold increase in revenue over the next 3 to 5 years.
Reiterated long-term guidance of a threefold increase in revenue in 3 to 5 years.
